text:
I do not know what suggestive graces

these villages of white little houses possess,

full of groves, full of ravines,

and fresh girls who rise early.


Quiet little villages, where the bell

of the old church sings for joy

when, beyond the mountain ridges,

the blushing morning laughs...


I do not know what innocent graces

these peaceful, quiet villages possess,

where grandmothers lull their grandchildren

inside the hammocks of the corridors...


Sweet little villages where cicadas

sing on the clear days of April,

while, by the fire of loving logs,

trembling guitars keep their tunes...


Peaceful corners where existence

runs gently, like pure water;

where even the winds, full of freshness,

carry notes of innocence on their wings...


I do not know what suggestive charms

these villages, soft as a nest, possess,

where sweet forgetfulness, sweet forgetfulness,

lays a rose-colored mantle over sorrows...

translation.title: Pueblan Airs
translation.editorial_note: The repeated village descriptions and refrain are preserved, with “pueblos” rendered variously as villages or little towns to retain the poem’s tender scale.
